title: DeepL API Pricing: Free vs Pro Plans (2026 Guide)
summary: DeepL API pricing is metered by characters, not requests or seats. Compare plans and calculate costs for your automation or integration needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden DeepL API Costs and Limits Teams Hit


Most surprises come from characters you didn't know you were paying for. What you send, how often you send it and how many languages you send it to shape the bill. Each trap below is a metering rule, not a price change.


### DeepL API Billing Traps That Inflate Character Counts


Translate one page into four languages and DeepL bills that page four times, so a source text of **10,000 characters becomes 40,000 billed characters** . DeepL meters characters, and it meters them per target language.


Adding a market multiplies spend rather than adding to it, which is why the choice of which languages to cover carries more weight than the per-million rate.


If a workflow resends a whole page every time one sentence changes, you pay for every character again. That is the second trap, retranslating unchanged text. Storing the previous translation and sending only the changed segments keeps the meter tied to edits, not to publishes.


### DeepL API HTML Markup and tag_handling Costs


Markup is the third. By default, HTML tags count as characters. In a[Drupal AI DeepL provider issue](https://www.drupal.org/project/ai_provider_deepl/issues/3632340) , DeepL billed the same HTML string at 229 characters without tag_handling.


Setting tag_handling to html, per the[same issue](https://www.drupal.org/project/ai_provider_deepl/issues/3632340) , brought it to 108 billed characters, because **tags aren't billed in that mode** , a saving of 121 characters. That's more than half the bill for this string.


On a content-heavy site, where much of each page is markup, the headline rate misleads. It overstates what you'd pay once tag_handling is on and understates what you pay when it's off.


**The takeaway is that one request parameter can move the effective rate more than negotiating a price, so set it before you estimate volume.**


### Request size, rate and glossary limits


Before you size batches, check the current limits in DeepL's API documentation. Request size, request rate and glossary size each cap how work can be split, and a pipeline that ignores them will fail or stall, not simply cost more.


Retried requests that partly succeed can also resend text you already paid for, so build retries around segments rather than whole documents.


### Cost-control settings DeepL provides


If a loop or a bulk import resends large volumes and nobody notices, an unbounded metered bill is exactly what you get.


DeepL lets you set a usage cap on an account, so spend stops at a ceiling you choose instead of running on, and that turns the bill into a bounded one.


On the Free plan, reaching the monthly character limit stops translation rather than charging overage, so the risk there is an outage, not a surprise invoice. Decide which failure you can tolerate, a stopped pipeline or a larger bill, and set the cap to match.


A DeepL cap only sees DeepL, though, and the loop that overspends usually lives in the tooling around it.

Its Ultimate plan adds SCIM, custom roles, audit logs, event streaming, git sync and releases, and SSO arrives with Team.


When a bulk import resends text, the record of what ran and who changed the flow sits in one place instead of several vendors' logs and bills. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.
